scope: The rule paraphrases and exact ISO locators below were checked against the locally supplied ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 text (ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.txt): PDF string-decoding/spacing interfaces, supported font dictionaries and embedding bindings, character selection, widths/CID metrics, PDF-specific CMap rules and ToUnicode. Every code-to-name slot of Standard, MacRoman, WinAnsi, PDFDoc, Symbol and ZapfDingbats was compared with Annex D; MacExpert was also checked. This is not verification of Adobe Glyph List rules, TN5014 grammar or external font-program binary formats. Provider additions were checked against ISO 9.6.2.2/Table 109 and 9.9.2, 9.8.1-9.8.2/Tables 120-121, 9.7.5.2/Table 116 and 9.10.2, and TN5014 sections 5.1-5.4 for pinned resource inheritance. AFM values and Unicode projection choices are checked against the pinned data files, not claimed as verification of external AFM or sfnt format standards. Recovery additions were checked against ISO 9.7.4.1 Table 115, 9.7.4.2, 9.7.5.4, 9.7.6.2, 9.10.3 and TN5014 7.4. Tolerant interpretations depart from those rules as individually reported below; corpus acceptance is evidence of tolerance, not standards conformance. Round 5 rechecks the PDF TrueType routes against 9.6.5.4 and Table 113 in the same local ISO text; final-paragraph alternatives are reader policy. Retained byte accounting is ADR 0012 policy, not a numerical requirement of Annex C.1. Substitution and optional-weight handling were checked against ISO 9.6.2.1-9.6.2.2, 9.6.5.2, 9.6.5.4, 9.8.1-9.8.2/Tables 120-121 and 9.9.2 in the same local text. Sixty-six Russian AFII name-to-scalar records were compared with local adobe-glyph-list data. Short aliases and invalid-weight discard are documented policies; full external AGL/AGLFN algorithm verification is not claimed. Horizontal CID substitution and Symbol/Dingbats additions were checked against the same local ISO text: 9.6.2.2, 9.6.5.2/Table 112, 9.6.5.4, 9.7.3/Table 114, 9.7.4.2-9.7.4.3, 9.7.5 and 9.10.2-9.10.3. CFF INDEX, DICT, charset layouts and standard SIDs used by the Foxit oracle were checked against local TN5176 sections 4, 5, 8-10, 13-14 and Appendix A. Regional OTF cmap expectations are independent binary-layout oracles; primary OpenType format review remains pending. Collection projection, Unicode subtable preference, horizontal-only substitutes and coalesced coverage diagnostics are explicit provider policies. Extraction additions were checked against the same local ISO text: 7.9.2.2, 9.3, 9.4.4, 9.10, 14.6, 14.8.2.5.1/14.8.2.5.3, 14.8.2.6.2 and 14.9.3-14.9.4. Trm and replacement/reversal semantics are normative; selection cells, untagged reading order, layout thresholds, word boundaries and search equivalence are explicitly reader policy. No Unicode normalization or full case-fold standard verification is claimed. Tagged extraction additions were checked against the same local ISO text: 7.9.7, 14.7.2-14.7.5 (Tables 354-359), 14.8.2.2, 14.8.4 and 14.9.3-14.9.4. Hierarchy order, owner lookup, roles, artifacts and replacement semantics are normative; separator serialization, unsupported namespace boundaries and retained byte accounting are explicit implementation policy. Standard namespace names, default namespace selection and role-set differences were checked against 14.8.6.1-14.8.6.2 and Annex M of the same text; logical depth-first order is defined by 14.8.2.5.1. Optional null dictionary values and indirect null were checked against 7.3.9, including structure keys, replacement properties and nonstructural null MCIDs. Reported structure fallback is ADR 0003/ADR 0014 reader recovery policy, not an additional normative ISO requirement; logical-structure fault locators remain those reviewed above. Two-view additions use the same primary ISO text: 12.5.3 (annotation flags), 14.6.2, 14.7.5.2-14.7.5.3 and 14.9.3-14.9.5. Page/logical API separation, fixed logical separator thresholds and reported metadata discard are documented reader policies. Strict rejection of nested ToUnicode parser/filter repairs was checked against ISO 7.3.5, 7.3.7, 7.4.4 and 9.10.3, with zlib integrity from RFC 1950 section 2.2; recovery-mode classification follows ADR 0003.

requirements.status: UTF-16BE ToUnicode and glyph-name fallback
requirements.gaps: The bundled provider supplies four Adobe collection Unicode projections; full AGL name data and the external naming algorithm review remain outside this subset.

verification.rule: ToUnicode takes priority, uses font-consistent code lengths and UTF-16BE sequences, increments the final bfrange byte, and uses only UseCMap from the stream dictionary.
verification.implementation: Valid ISO ToUnicode rules agree. Strict font loading rejects malformed interpretations; repair mode retains drawable glyphs and reports repairs. Repair mode preserves unambiguous Unicode as specified in text-tounicode-recovery.

verification.verdict: ISO subset agrees after corrections

Unrecognized name components contribute no Unicode, and entirely unknown names return None; this external AGL algorithm remains pending primary-text review.

verification.verdict: ISO subset agrees after corrections
choices: Invalid strings ending before the chosen codespace length consume the remaining bytes.
Local CMap mappings override inherited mappings; later local definitions override earlier ones. The full TN5014 rule is pending primary-text review.

requirements.gaps: External font-program interpretation remains delegated; map entries are checked for usable glyph selectors during decoding.

requirements.gaps: Text-state operators, BT/ET and positioning now belong to pagura-interpret; painting belongs to pagura-paint. These remain outside this registry's PDF binding tests; earlier verification records retain their historical crate names.

verification.verdict: ISO decoder interface agrees; text-state operator execution remains in pagura-render

requirements.status: Symbolic or unencoded fonts use direct symbol/Mac codes; encoded nonsymbolic fonts use names via Unicode, Mac OS Roman, then post.
requirements.gaps: Full AGL algorithm primary-text review remains pending; the exact cmap API distinction is now implemented upstream and covered here.

verification.rule: Symbolic or unencoded fonts use direct symbol/Mac codes; encoded nonsymbolic fonts use names via Unicode, Mac OS Roman, then post.
verification.implementation: ISO selection routes implemented with distinct Windows BMP, full-Unicode and platform-0 API variants.
verification.expectations: Normative routes and Table 113 agree with independent glyph-ID expectations. Additional mappings are explicit reader policy permitted by the final paragraph, not normative fallback orders.
verification.verdict: ISO 9.6.5.4 and Table 113 routes agree; final-paragraph choices are separately documented and tested.
choices: When symbolic/no-Encoding wording overlaps the named/Nonsymbolic wording, the more specific direct-code paragraph takes precedence.

Use the prescribed name route and post before reader-chosen fallbacks. After failure try Mac OS Roman by glyph name, full Windows Unicode (3,10), platform 0 Unicode, then the symbol byte route. Never use ToUnicode to select a glyph.
The four allowed symbol high-byte ranges are tried in ascending order; a conforming symbol cmap uses one range.
When Mac OS Roman contains aliases for a name, the lowest character code is used.

For direct codes, try symbol high-byte variants, then Mac Roman. Only after failure try (3,1), (3,10), then platform 0; within each Unicode table try the literal byte before F000/F100/F200 offsets. Missing all routes selects glyph 0. Multi-scalar names never select a scalar cmap entry.
A successful post lookup is binding even for glyph 0; reader fallback applies only when lookup fails.

legacy_post_review.rule: The 0x00025000 version stores one signed byte offset per glyph into standard Macintosh names. This is a deprecated, documented layout, not post 3.0 absence of names.
legacy_post_review.scope: Paired original post 2.5/2.0 programs share cmap, outlines and metrics; PDF 9.6.5.4 determines direct Unicode and glyph-name fallback. Head 6ac4b1d27 passed all 13 integrated Pagura render controls in hosted run40385518384 and full three-platform checks in run40385513689. This is scoped evidence, not font-family parity.

cmap8_review.rule: Format 8 contains an 8192-byte bitmap, sorted nonoverlapping sequential map groups and a reserved zero word. Its introductory UTF-16 description conflicts with the later U+0000..U+0010 high-word illustration. Both supplementary encodings remain diagnostic candidates until adjudicated; BMP coverage is unaffected by that ambiguity.
cmap8_review.scope: Six original subjects with matched format-12 controls, unchanged outlines/metrics and independent rectangle expectations. Post 3 removes name fallback. FontFile2 PDF Differences selects A or u1F600 through the existing binding. No product change or support claim.
cmap8_review.observation_caution: The first supplementary subjects map the literal byte and supplementary scalar to the same glyph, so their MuPDF passes establish admission but cannot distinguish selection routes. Follow-up isolated rows map the literal byte to a different curved glyph. No earlier bytes/oracles are changed.

requirements.status: PDF font descriptors bind Type1, TrueType, CFF and CID CFF programs; PDF widths supply advances and program matrices transform outlines.
requirements.gaps: Type1/CFF/Type2 primary texts are now available locally but binary verification is delegated to pagura-font; this registry covers PDF bindings. PDF binding kind and declared length extents are checked; Type1 Length1/2 boundaries are not independently reconciled with parsed eexec boundaries, and OpenType outline technology is not independently classified here.

verification.rule: PDF font descriptors bind Type1, TrueType, CFF and CID CFF programs; PDF widths supply advances and program matrices transform outlines.

requirements.status: Bounded, reported tolerance with independent strict and repaired oracles
requirements.gaps: The repaired interpretation is compatibility policy, not a claim that malformed input conforms.

verification.rule: ToUnicode controls extraction, independently of glyph selection. Sources in simple fonts use one byte, destinations use UTF-16BE, and bfrange increments may not overflow the final byte.
verification.implementation: Normative departures are rejected with a repair tag in strict interpretation and reported before tolerant use.
verification.expectations: Independently authored Python fixtures give strict error tags and exact repaired glyph IDs, widths, matrices and Unicode; no Rust output is used. Pixel fixtures independently calculate the same rectangle in actual rendered pages.
verification.verdict: Normative checks and explicit repair policy agree with the independent fixtures.
choices: Reject malformed extraction data when the font's Unicode is loaded for text extraction under Strict, preserving the original error and refused repair tag without reporting an applied repair. Repair mode keeps drawable glyphs and other Unicode fallback methods. Rendering never loads ToUnicode (ADR 0034), so its faults neither fail nor repair a rendering.
Repair two-byte simple-font source codes by their low byte, preserving agreeing aliases and dropping conflicting aliases.
Omit invalid UTF-16 destinations atomically, including malformed surrogate sequences and odd byte counts. An invalid child definition suppresses inherited text for that source.
Repair overflowing bfrange strings with big-endian byte carry. Keep valid UTF-16 results, omit invalid ones, and stop at full-string overflow without wrapping.

On other malformed, unsupported, cyclic or budget-exceeding ToUnicode data, Strict propagates the original error. Repair discards the whole map and reports font.tounicode-invalid or the original repair tag. Existing parser and output budgets remain enforced.

choices: Repair a missing CIDToGIDMap with Identity; explicit unusable maps still fail.

Interpret an otherwise reversed byte bound as an integer interval, split into disjoint aligned rectangular pieces without widening it. Reversed whole intervals, conflicting codespaces and ambiguous code lengths remain errors.
Strict mode rejects these painting-critical repairs with their stable tags. ToUnicode maps also reject in Strict; only Repair may discard unusable maps.

requirements.status: PdfFont::retained_bytes is a saturating, constant-time retained-storage estimate computed once when loading succeeds (ADR 0012 policy).
requirements.gaps: Estimate only, not allocator telemetry or peak bound. Provider programs remain excluded; CIDToGIDMap capacity is counted separately.

verification.rule: Annex C.1 discusses processor limits; the retained accounting amounts and provider ownership convention are implementation policy under ADR 0012.
verification.implementation: Owned encoding payloads, widths, vertical metrics, CMaps, Unicode, CIDToGIDMap, Type 3 resources/procedures and FontProgram::retained_bytes plus handle/Arc overhead are computed once. Names include payload allowances; trees add 64 bytes per entry. Provider-owned shared resources are excluded and remain its cache-budget responsibility.
verification.expectations: Unit tests cover all five requested font categories, owned resource growth, stable repeated reads, shared provider identity/Unicode exclusion and saturating arithmetic. No allocator-accurate size is claimed. Exact program-retained accounting and separate CID-map capacity are tested for embedded TrueType, CFF, Type 1 and composite programs.
verification.verdict: Accounting policy tested, not an ISO-defined byte count.
choices: Include the PdfFont struct itself, but exclude Document-owned source dictionaries/streams and renderer-owned outlines. Replace the renderer input-size estimate with retained_bytes; do not add the two.

Provider substitute programs, predefined CMaps and CID-to-Unicode tables are charged by their provider, never per font. Copied encodings/metrics, embedded maps and inherited map copies remain owned allocations.
Embedded programs count FontProgram::retained_bytes plus the FontProgram handle and two usize Arc counters. Substituted provider programs are excluded; CID map capacity remains separate.

requirements.status: Short Latin family/style aliases use bundled metric-compatible outlines; Russian AFII names select the corresponding glyphs rather than .notdef.

requirements.status: Invalid optional FontWeight used for substitution is a strict tagged rejection or reported repair; Repair ignores the hint and uses normal weight.

verification.implementation: Invalid numeric or nonnumeric weights are rejected with font.descriptor-weight in Strict; Repair reports the ignored hint, keeps the normal substitution default and preserves independent style flags.
verification.expectations: Minimized strict/repaired fixtures give independent glyph IDs, text, matrices, selected font data and unchanged PDF widths. The corpus uses invalid value 0, including Cyrillic Differences.

choices: Do not round or clamp invalid weights into another style. Ignore the invalid optional value and use normal weight 400, retaining Italic, Serif, FixedPitch and ForceBold selection.

Coordinates precede page Rotate, UserUnit and device scaling. Hidden optional content and all render modes remain in raw glyphs. Pattern cells, masks, Type 3 internals and annotation appearances are paint constructions, excluded from page semantics.

choices: Without a structure tree, Outermost marked occurrences keep content order as indivisible blocks. Other blocks cluster by one-degree orientation in discovery order, inline start anchors within 1.5 em into columns, then perpendicular baseline descending. Horizontal columns run left to right; vertical columns run right to left.

Baselines within .35 perpendicular em and direction dot product above .98 form lines. Displacements over 2.5 em split fragments. Positive unoccupied gaps above .2 perpendicular em insert spaces; ReversedChars occurrences rely on explicit whitespace. Line displacements over 1.8 em, column shifts over 2.5 em or orientation changes insert paragraph breaks. These thresholds are configurable except the documented clustering constants.

Words are alphanumeric/underscore runs, not UAX 29 segmentation. Unknown Unicode exports U+FFFD but remains None and cannot match a literal replacement character. Hidden optional content is excluded by default; render mode 3, clip-only and clipped text stay extractable. Negative sizes and rotated baselines use their signed writing vectors.

requirements.status: Bounded logical /K preorder is an optional assistive-technology view; geometric page text, search and selection remain unchanged on tagged pages.

verification.rule: The structure hierarchy associates content with ordered children; RoleMap applies even to standard names, and valid role-map loops terminate when recognised or revisited. Marked and structure-element artifacts do not contribute real logical text.
verification.implementation: Iterative, budgeted hierarchy traversal validates parent relationships and rejects repeated structural nodes. Role names are retained; recognised standard types include arbitrary positive Hn headings without leading zeros. The default PDF 1.7 namespace and explicitly registered PDF 1.7/PDF 2.0 namespaces distinguish standard role sets; known explicit namespaces do not use the root RoleMap. Optional null-valued dictionary entries, including indirect null, are absent under 7.3.9; null K entries contribute no children. The result is LogicalText, separate from the geometric page view. Its characters map to source glyph ranges and structure-element ranges index logical UTF-8 bytes.
verification.expectations: Independent Python-authored /K graphs and ParentTree arrays, recursive logical text/ranges and declared FontMatrix/origin quad arithmetic; malformed outcomes are authored from the violated requirement. Never obtained from Rust output.
verification.verdict: Reviewed against local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 text; supported subset and independent expectations agree. Layout separators and accounting amounts are reader policy.
choices: A successfully processed structure root supplies only TextPage::logical(); it never reorders or removes page text. Unknown roles and valid unrecognised cycles preserve names in generic structures. MarkInfo/Marked documents require recognised roles; faults use reported fallback in repair mode.

Logical separators use default layout thresholds, independently of page layout options; paragraphs/headings use two LFs and list/table cells one LF. with_layout retains the same immutable logical allocation and fallback cause. Hidden optional content stays excluded from the logical view.

Custom namespaces and RoleMapNS currently make structure order unavailable (text.structure-namespace), with reported geometric fallback in repair mode. The two standard namespaces without RoleMapNS are supported; absent NS uses PDF 1.7, even in a PDF 2.0 file. This is not a PDF/UA validator or complete accessibility model.

requirements.status: Page/form-local MCID identity and whole-object references checked against the bounded ParentTree number-tree reader.

verification.rule: An integer child uses its element Pg; MCR supplies MCID, optional Stm and overriding Pg. OBJR supplies an object and page. StructParents indexes an MCID-to-owner array; StructParent indexes a whole-object owner. These keys are mutually exclusive.

requirements.status: ADR 0003 / ADR 0014 recovery policy: unusable optional structure yields no logical view and a reported fallback in repair mode, leaving the entire geometric page view intact; strict mode rejects text.structure-fallback.

verification.implementation: Logical export builds a separate immutable result; page text is never mutated. Repair mode retains geometric characters, copy text, lines, words and quads, exposes no logical view, retains the original typed failure and reports its original reason, feature tag, object and position. Strict mode rejects with the stable repair tag. Compilation, unrelated unsupported features, resource and budget errors propagate unchanged. Optional hierarchy traversal stops at its configured depth and falls back without visiting deeper nodes; this is distinguished by typed failure provenance from parser, number-tree, compilation and general work/storage limits, which remain errors.
verification.expectations: Independent Python cell arithmetic supplies exact geometric fallback text, separate from the independently authored logical /K graph. Each malformed or unsupported vector checks both recovery modes, underlying cause, diagnostic and complete geometric character/line/word preservation and logical-view absence. The deep-tree vector checks bounded fallback at the hierarchy depth cap; independent tests retain compilation and general work-budget failures as unrepaired Limit errors in both recovery modes.

choices: Diagnostic strings are fixed and preserve feature tags without allocating unbounded formatted messages. TextPage::structure_fallback exposes the original typed error independently of the bounded/deduplicated document diagnostic sink.

Parser, capture, number-tree, work and storage resource limits remain errors in both recovery modes. Optional hierarchy-depth exhaustion abandons only logical ordering at the configured cap, preserving already-constructed geometric text. No deeper nodes are visited and no budget is raised. verification.rule: Dictionary keys are names; names begin with a solidus. Flate streams use the zlib wrapper, whose Adler-32 verifies decoded data (RFC 1950 section 2.2). repair_policy.behaviour: Reject unusable extraction data in Strict; discard and report it in Repair without changing glyph selection.
In repair mode use low bytes of two-byte simple-font sources; conflicting aliases have unknown Unicode. Strict rejects font loading with the original error and refused repair tag.

In repair mode omit invalid destinations, retaining unaffected entries and blocking invalid child overrides from resurrecting parent values. Strict rejects font loading with the original error and refused repair tag.
In repair mode increment with big-endian carry, retaining valid destinations until full-string overflow; never wrap. Strict rejects font loading with the original error and refused repair tag.
Accept counts above 100 within existing budgets only after permission to repair.
Split malformed rectangular bounds into an exact integer interval, accepting only non-overlapping, unambiguous pieces.
Assume Identity when the required embedded Type2 CIDFont map is missing, after permission to repair.
While choosing an unknown non-embedded Latin face, report and ignore an invalid optional weight, preserving normal default 400 and independent descriptor flags. Strict rejects with the tag.
